name: joint ownership keeps two simultaneous owner edges active
description: Shared/joint ownership: 'Lena and I co-own the lake cabin' is TWO owner edges -- Me.owns->Cabin and Lena.owns->Cabin -- that must BOTH stay active (accumulate, not supersede). They land on different identity keys (different subject/entity), so even the newest-wins state path cannot collide them. Pins docs/reference/ANALYSIS.md 'property graph': ownership is a relationship/state edge between an owner entity and a thing; co-ownership is two such edges to one thing. Emitted as state kind to show the per-subject key keeps them apart regardless of kind; one provisional Place entity (Cabin) carries two inbound edges.
xfail: The co-ownership SHARE is dropped. Both edges carry `value_json` {share: joint}, and an edge written through assert_fact stores no value_json at all - `object` is the object entity, so the literal renderer never runs. What survives is two `owns` edges to one Place, which is the scenario's headline; what is gone is the one field that says the ownership is JOINT rather than two rival claims to the same cabin. ACCEPTED as designed, not open. `assert_fact.object` is a plain STRING and there is no structured `value_json` field: TOOL_SURFACE gap 5's deliberate narrowing, the model is never asked to nest. So a literal is stored as {value} or {value, unit} and anything richer is flattened by runner._object_literal first, while an edge with an object entity stores no value_json at all. W5 MUST NOT DELETE: `facts.value_json`, `_quantity_value`'s unit split, or `supersession.values_equal`'s cross-unit comparison - the EMR importer and the projections write and read structured values through the non-model path.

steps.body: Lena and I co-own the lake cabin now.
